verdict: ROAS dropped sharply this week; zero purchases recorded over the last six days.
narrative: This period, your Meta ads delivered 22 purchases and a 28-day return on ad spend (ROAS) of 3.61 — but that number masks a harder reality: the last six days produced zero recorded purchases while daily spend held steady at roughly $53. The drop is a revenue-per-dollar problem, not a spending problem. Conversion signals from Shopify are also firing inconsistently, so some purchases may be under-reported; that tracking issue is being resolved now. Alongside this, organic visibility softened — Google Business Profile engagement fell 32% week-over-week and Instagram reach declined — pointing to broader demand softness rather than a single isolated cause. Ad creative is being refreshed this week, and the funnel test and UTM tracking are on track to close by August 31, which will give us a cleaner read on true purchase volume going into September.

highlights.phrase: 28-day return on ad spend — down 60% from the prior week, driven by a purchase stall in the back half of the period.
Purchases recorded in the last six days, against an average of roughly 1.3 per day before that stretch.
Google Business Profile actions this period — calls, direction requests, and site clicks from local search.

watch_item.issue: Purchases have gone to zero over the last six days while ad spend continued; conversion tracking is also returning unreliable signals from Shopify.
watch_item.fix: Conversion tracking is being repaired now, and ad creative is being refreshed this week to address the performance drop — both actions are already in motion ahead of the August 31 funnel close.
